content.title: Artemis II crew in 'great spirits' as NASA shares first look from space
content.text: WASHINGTON (TNND) — The Artemis II crew is expected to reach the lunar surface and orbit the moon by Monday as the mission continues to perform "well." Lakiesha Hawkins, Acting Deputy Associate Administrator of NASA’s Exploration Systems, said the mission continues to perform “well” overall and the crew is in “great spirits," during a NASA press briefing on Friday.As of 3:30 p.m. E.T. on Friday, Hawkins said the crew is more than 100,000 miles from Earth and 150,000 miles from the moon.Judd Frieling, Artemis II Ascent Flight Director, said the crew was able to talk to their families on Friday morning. Hawkins emphasized that the crew has been very busy on their journey.The crew is also getting a unique look at planet Earth as the astronauts' journey continues toward the moon on Friday. NASA released the crew's first images on Friday, just one and a half days into the first astronaut moonshot in over 50 years.One of the photos, taken by commander Reid Wiseman, shows a slice of Earth from one of the Orion capsule's windows. Another photo shows the entire plant, where you can see the oceans and clouds above.Chattanooga Navy commander returns home to share lessons with studentsHoward Hu, Orion Program Manager, said on Saturday, the crew plans to have the “biggest selfie stick in the world” for a photo moment.Once the astronauts reach the moon, the crew will slingshot around it in the capsule, make a U-turn and head back home to Earth.On Thursday night, the astronauts fired the Orion capsule's main engine, or translunar injection (TLI), which set them on course to the moon. "With that successful TLI, the crew’s feeling pretty good up here on our way to the moon," Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen said. "And we just wanted to communicate to everyone around the planet who’s worked to making Artemis possible that we firmly felt the power of you perseverance during every second of that burn. Humanity has once again shown what we are capable of and it’s your hopes for the future that carry us now on this journey around the moon."Along with Canada's Hansen, NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch make up the Artemis II crew. It is the first lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972. NASA will follow this mission with Artemis III, staying closer to Earth to test Orion's ability to dock with one or both of the new lunar landers being developed. It won't be until at least 2028 that NASA follows up with Artemis IV, which will return humans to the moon's surface. And after that? NASA plans to begin building a $20 billion lunar base with rovers, habitats and other infrastructure. The agency is targeting the lunar south pole for the base into the 2030s. ________Editor's Note: The Associated Press and The National News Desk's Maria Tedesco contributed to this report.
